newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RESEARCH ALERT - UBS starts Banco Frances as buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - UBS starts Banco Frances as buy.

text.p: - UBS Securities said Thursday it initiated coverage of Argentina's Banco Frances with a "buy" rating because of its "excellent" fundamentals and expansion plans.
- It said operating earnings were likely to grow around 20 percent while price/earnings ratios were nearly half that level.

- "BFR has a rock solid balance sheet; its capital is nearly 15 percent of assets, and operating returns are in excess of two percent on assets. Asset quality is improving owning to a nearly 20 percent decline in past due loans", UBS said in a report.

- It said loan demand reflects both cyclical economic strength and increasing consumer confidence and market penetration, encouraged by better banking service, pricing and improved delivery procedures.

- "As the oldest private bank in Argentina, BFR's relationships confer a competitive advantage. It has considerable equity investments and minority interests worth in excess of $200 million over cost, adding about $4.00 to stated book value of $16," UBS said.
- The bank's expansion of over 50 branches in the next 18 months should be viewed as enhancing the value of the franchise, with a higher quality and stronger earnings growth prospects.
- These factors, compounded with a bank as strong and well regarded as Frances whose stock is suffering in the present market downdraft, make it a great buying opportunity.
- "We project a price target of $35 per ADS, or slightly above its pre-Tequila high of $32 and about 14 times projected 1998 fiscal earnings," UBS said.
